Dear Members of the Search Committee,

I am writing to express my interest in inclusion in the pool for Part-Time Faculty in Economics within the Department of Economics at DePaul University’s Driehaus College of Business. I am currently a Ph.D. candidate in Economics at George Mason University and hold an M.A. in Economics. Since 2021, I have served as a Graduate Lecturer, acting as instructor of record for multiple undergraduate economics courses, and I meet the qualifications for undergraduate and graduate instruction outlined in the posting.

My teaching experience includes Principles of Macroeconomics, Intermediate Microeconomics, Economics of Developing Areas, and International Economic Policy. While I have taught across fields, my strongest areas are microeconomics, development economics, and economic history. I am particularly comfortable teaching introductory and intermediate microeconomics as well as development-oriented courses that emphasize institutions, policy, and empirical evidence. All of my prior teaching has been at the undergraduate level, and I have independently designed syllabi, assessments, and course materials.

I have taught both in-person and online courses and am accustomed to adapting content and pacing to different instructional formats and academic calendars. This experience prepares me well for DePaul’s quarter system, including intensive summer offerings, and for the fluctuating instructional needs typical of part-time appointments.

My research training is in economic history and political economy, with an emphasis on institutions, development, and media. Although my primary interest in this position is teaching, my research background informs my pedagogy by grounding economic theory in historical and applied contexts that resonate with business and policy-focused students.

I would welcome the opportunity to contribute to the Department of Economics by teaching courses aligned with departmental needs as they arise throughout the academic year. Thank you for considering my application. I would be happy to provide any additional materials and to discuss how my teaching experience could support the instructional mission of the Driehaus College of Business.

Sincerely,
Patrick J. Crawford
